Particle accelerator technology developed for fusion experiments is now used in medical imaging and cancer treatment, helping millions of patients. Superconducting magnets engineered for fusion reactors have advanced MRI machines, making diagnostics more accessible for communities. Plasma physics knowledge has improved industrial processes like semiconductor manufacturing, boosting the global tech economy. The iritic nature of these cross-disciplinary breakthroughs shows how fundamental science ripples into everyday life. Fusion R&D has also trained generations of physicists and engineers who now lead innovations in renewable energy.
